channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Texan shot dead by ICE agent months before killings in Minneapolis, records show
item.description: The involvement of federal immigration agents in the fatal shooting of Ruben Ray Martinez on South Padre Island in March had not been disclosed in initial reports.

item.title: Tariff reversal and Houston (Feb. 23, 2026)
item.description: On Monday's show: We discuss how the Supreme Court’s decision to strike down many of President Trump’s tariffs might affect Greater Houston. And a group of reporters discusses some of the latest education news affecting our area.

item.title: Democratic early voting surges in Texas primary election, far outpacing 2022
item.description: Compared with the same point in 2022, Democratic early voting is up by roughly 211,000 ballots, while Republican turnout has increased by about 6,000.

item.title: Hello Houston (February 23, 2026)
item.description: Today: We break down the races and propositions in the 2026 primary election, learn about National Eating Disorders Awareness Week, and talk with the team behind the Barbara Jordan documentary, “The Inquisitor.”

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (February 23, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Houston rodeo celebrations get underway with food, wine competition featuring thousands of entries
item.description: Thousands of cowboy-boot-clad visitors packed NRG Center on Sunday evening for the competition that named several local restaurants and wine vendors best in class.

item.title: Camp Mystic parents sue state, accusing Texas officials of failing to enforce evacuation plan requirement
item.description: A group of parents whose children died in the July 4 floods claim in a federal lawsuit that Camp Mystic’s emergency instructions directed kids to stay in cabins even though state law requires evacuation plans for camps.

item.title: Houston nonprofits urge SNAP beneficiaries to prepare for changes to work requirements
item.description: The expanded work requirements require recipients to work or attend training for 80 hours a month.

item.title: Businesses could spend years waiting for tariff refunds in wake of SCOTUS decision, experts say
item.description: The University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School estimates the U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling that the Trump administration illegally collected emergency tariffs means businesses are due up to $175 billion in refunds. The administration is likely to fight those cases in court.

item.title: Report finds 2024 fatal Deer Park hydrogen sulfide release caused by labeling, protocol issues
item.description: The leading cause of the incident was a lack of proper identification of the piping, the board found. While the refinery provided drawings and lists of the flanges, they were not sufficient to help workers tell the difference between “nearly identical segments,” according to a news release from the board.
